title: Sexual and asexual reproduction

match.reason: No single bank point teaches the brief's contrast of both strategies: the asexual and sexual cards each cover only one side, and the advantages card is about trade-offs rather than the mechanism, and the Victorian Units 1 and 2 cards go deeper than Year 9.

draft.title: Sexual and asexual reproduction
card: One parent makes new organisms. The offspring have the same genes as the parent, so they are identical to it and to each other.
Two gametes, which are sex cells, join to form a new organism. Usually one gamete comes from each parent.
Each gamete carries a different mix of genes, so the offspring get a new combination. They are not identical to their parents or to each other.
Bacteria splitting in two is asexual. A dog and a rose bush making seeds from two parents is sexual.
draft.remember: One parent gives identical offspring. Two gametes give offspring that vary.

a.q: A strawberry plant grows a new plant from a runner on its stem. Why is the new plant identical to its parent?
opts: One parent made it, so it has the same genes
Two gametes joined, so it has the same genes
It grew from a seed, so it has the same genes
Two parents shared genes, so it has the same genes
a.why: A runner is made by one parent without gametes joining, so the new plant gets the parent's genes. Two gametes joining mixes genes and gives offspring that vary, so that is wrong here.
a.clue: Count the parents and ask if gametes joined.

b.q: Two brown mice in Darwin have a litter of four. The pups differ in colour and size. What best explains this?
opts: Each pup came from two gametes with different gene mixes
Each pup came from one parent splitting in two
Each pup copied the genes of one parent exactly
Each pup grew differently only because of its food
b.why: Pups form when two gametes join, and each gamete carries a different mix of genes, so offspring vary. One parent copying itself would give identical offspring. Food may affect size, but it does not explain the variation in a whole litter on its own.
b.clue: Think about what joins to make each pup.

a.best: One parent made it, so it has the same genes

b.best: Each pup came from two gametes with different gene mixes

problems.detail: "A dog and a rose bush making seeds from two parents is sexual" can be read as saying a dog makes seeds. Separate the two examples, for example: "A dog having puppies and a rose bush making seeds are both sexual."

Question a uses strawberry runners, which belong to point 3 (Reproduction in flowering plants). The why also explains how a runner forms. The card never says runners are asexual, so the student has to bring in an idea from another point.

proposal.title: Sexual and asexual reproduction
card: One parent makes new organisms, with no gametes joining. The offspring have the same genes as the parent, so they are identical to it and to each other.
Two gametes, which are sex cells, join to form a new organism. Usually one gamete comes from each parent.
Each gamete carries a different mix of genes, so the offspring get a new combination. They are not identical to their parents or to each other.
Bacteria splitting in two is asexual. A dog having puppies and a rose bush making seeds are both sexual.
proposal.remember: One parent gives identical offspring. Two gametes give offspring that vary.

a.q: A bacterium in a pond splits into two new cells. Why are the two new cells identical to each other?
opts: One parent made them, so they share its genes
Two gametes joined, so they share the same genes
Each got a new mix of genes from two parents
Each gamete carried the same mix of genes
a.why: Splitting in two is asexual: one parent makes the new cells with no gametes joining, so both get the parent's genes. Gametes joining would mix genes and give offspring that vary, so that cannot explain identical cells.
a.clue: Count the parents and ask if gametes joined.

b.q: Two brown mice in Darwin have a litter of four. The pups differ in colour and size. What best explains this?
opts: Each pup got a new mix of genes from two gametes
Each pup came from one parent splitting in two
Each pup copied the genes of one parent exactly
Each pup got the same genes from both parents
b.why: Each pup forms when two gametes join, and each gamete carries a different mix of genes, so the pups vary. One parent copying itself would give identical offspring, so that cannot explain pups that differ.
b.clue: Think about what joins to make each pup.

problems.detail: 'One parent gives identical offspring' is neater than the card. The card defines asexual as one parent with no gametes joining, and says gametes 'usually' come from two parents, so one parent can reproduce sexually (e.g. self-pollination) and give varied offspring. Saying 'One parent, no gametes joining, gives identical offspring' would match the card.
